newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds off modestly with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds off modestly with Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities slipped somewhat on Wednesday, generally matching a decline in Treasuries prices.
Fifteen-year pass-throughs outperformed 30-year paper, traders said. "There seem to be some pretty decent bids in 15-year," said one trader based in New York.
Overall, mortgages generally were unchanged to off 3/32, with discount coupons falling furthest.
Pass-throughs dipped early on Wednesday after the Labor Department said producer prices rose 0.4 percent in October, up from a 0.2 percent gain in September.
"Energy prices moved sharply higher in the period, but I think people will view that as temporary," said Dan Seto, senior economist at Nikko Securities Co International Inc.
The core Producer Price Index, which excludes volatile food and energy components, shrank 0.3 percent last month. It had risen 0.3 in September.

By late on Wednesday, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5-percent coupons were off 1/32 at 100-24/32, yielding 124 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Maes were off 2/32 at 100-17/32, and Freddie Mac 7.5s had slipped 1/32 to 100-24/32.
